rows.selection_reason: No experiments are completed yet, so there is no evidence about which modality, encoder, profile setting, or fusion strategy is most important. This experiment establishes a minimal RNA-only, single-profile baseline using a simple PCA representation, which will anchor later comparisons of multiprofile aggregation, learned RNA encoders, image-only models, and multimodal fusion. It is the best first use of budget because it is simple, interpretable, and reduces uncertainty about the baseline performance of the RNA representation before testing more complex designs.

The only completed experiment is a moderate-performing RNA-only, single-profile PCA baseline, so it is still unclear whether a learned RNA representation can improve over PCA. config_004 keeps model setting, single-profile, and no aggregation/fusion fixed while changing only the RNA encoder to scvi_n200, directly testing the effect of RNA representation. This is the best next experiment because it isolates one key design choice with minimal confounds before adding multiprofile aggregation or image fusion.

The completed RNA-only singleprofile experiments show that scvi_n200 outperforms pca_n2000 on both accuracy and F1, suggesting scvi is the more promising RNA representation. However, it is still unclear whether using multiple profiles with aggregation improves performance over a single profile. config_005 keeps the best-performing RNA encoder and changes only the profile setting and aggregation to multiprofile with simple avgpool, isolating the effect of multiprofile aggregation. This is a high-value next experiment because it exploits the current best RNA direction while testing an important untested design choice before adding image or transformer complexity.

config_005 shows a large gain for scvi_n200 + multiprofile + avgpool, but this single result conflates the scvi representation with the multiprofile/avgpool setting. config_002 keeps profile and aggregation fixed and changes only the RNA encoder to pca_n2000, directly isolating whether the gain depends on scvi or whether multiprofile+avgpool alone is sufficient. This is the best next use of budget because it reduces a key representation uncertainty with a one-factor comparison from the strongest setup, guiding whether to use a simpler PCA representation before adding image or fusion.

Existing evidence shows multiprofile RNA with scvi_n200 and avgpool is the strongest completed setting (0.650 acc, 0.628 F1), and scvi_n200 also outperforms pca_n2000 in both single- and multiprofile RNA-only models. The key uncertainty is whether transformer aggregation can improve over avgpool for the best RNA encoder. config_006 tests this by changing only aggregation from avgpool to transformer while keeping rna_only, multiprofile, and scvi_n200 fixed, making it a clean comparison and a high-value use of the next experiment.

RNA multiprofile scvi_n200 is currently best, but avgpool and transformer are nearly tied, so the transformer gain is not yet reliable. config_003 tests PCA multiprofile with transformer, completing the encoder/aggregation factorial and clarifying whether aggregation matters across encoders. This is a minimal, low-confounding next step that reduces uncertainty about aggregation before introducing image or fusion changes.

The completed RNA-only experiments show that multiprofile with avgpool is a strong, simple regime, with the best accuracy and F1 from scvi_n200 multiprofile avgpool/transformer, but there is still no evidence that image features are informative under that same regime. config_011 tests an image-only ResNet50 baseline with multiprofile avgpool, matching the profile and aggregation of the best RNA setting. This is the best next experiment because it is simpler than any multimodal fusion configuration, avoids introducing fusion or a second image encoder, and provides a direct baseline for later isolating the effect of adding RNA and fusion.

RNA-only multiprofile scvi_n200 is currently strong (≈0.65 accuracy/F1), but image evidence is sparse and weak: ResNet50 multiprofile avgpool reaches only 0.328 accuracy/0.288 F1. The key uncertainty is whether image performance is limited by the ResNet50 encoder or by a general lack of useful image signal. config_014 tests this by swapping in ImageNet ViT-L while keeping multiprofile and avgpool fixed, giving a clean comparison to config_011. This is the best next budget use because it isolates image representation, avoids jumping to multimodal fusion, and will clarify whether image modality is worth pursuing in later multimodal experiments.

The strongest evidence so far is that RNA-only multiprofile scvi_n200 with avgpool or transformer aggregation performs best, while image-only multiprofile avgpool is weak, with imagenet_vit_l slightly better than resnet50 on F1. The main uncertainty is whether adding image features to the strong RNA baseline improves performance. config_036 tests this with a simple concat fusion while holding the RNA encoder, profile setting, and aggregation fixed, and it uses the image encoder with the better image-only F1. This makes it the most informative next experiment for isolating the contribution of image fusion before trying more complex fusion or alternative RNA encoders.

The strongest result so far is config_036, a multimodal multiprofile model using scvi_n200, imagenet_vit_l, avgpool, and concat fusion, with validation accuracy 0.715 and F1 0.687. RNA-only results show multiprofile and scvi representations are promising, while image-only models are much weaker, so the main remaining uncertainty is how the RNA and image features should be combined. config_037 tests weighted fusion while keeping all other design choices identical to config_036, directly isolating the effect of fusion. This is an efficient one-factor extension of the current best direction: it can either improve performance or confirm that concat is the better fusion choice without confounding the result with changes to encoder, profile setting, or aggregation.
